title: A builder for many optional settings

blocks.text: A class with many optional parameters ends up with a tangle of overloaded constructors. The page's cure is the **Builder pattern**: the required values go to the builder's constructor, each optional one has its own method, and `build()` checks everything once and creates the object.
Write `Order` and its nested static class `Order.Builder`:

items: `Order.builder(String customer)` returns a builder. The customer is required: `null` throws `NullPointerException`.
`quantity(int)`, `note(String)` and `express(boolean)` each set one option and return the same builder, so calls can be chained.
`build()` returns the `Order`, and refuses a quantity below `1` with `IllegalArgumentException`.
`Order` has the getters `getCustomer()`, `getQuantity()`, `getNote()` and `isExpress()`, and no public constructor.

blocks.text:
Order.builder("Ann").quantity(3).note("ring twice").express(true).build()
    -> Ann, 3, "ring twice", express
Order.builder("Ann").build()           -> Ann, 1, "", not express
Order.builder("Ann").quantity(0).build() -> IllegalArgumentException

cases.says: A builder with every option set builds an order carrying each of them.
Options that were never set take their defaults: quantity 1, an empty note, not express.
build refuses a quantity below 1 with IllegalArgumentException.
Starting a builder with a null customer throws NullPointerException.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A class with many optional parameters is created through a builder whose build method checks the result once.
